title: The Board Wants a Word
subject: Jensen Huang
parody: Parody. Every statement, headline and reaction in this game is invented. Not affiliated with or endorsed by anyone depicted.

setup.headline: The board wants a word.
setup.dek: A leaked memo says the board is "reviewing leadership". Cameras are camped outside HQ. You write what he says next. Five questions. Every word gets printed.

character.name: Jensen
character.source: Higgsfield: GPT Image 2.6 caricature per expression -> Tripo H3.1 image-to-3D (2026-11-16)

options.text: Fake news. I have never been more in charge.
headlines: Board members screenshot 'never more in charge'
Leaked minutes contradict CEO within the hour
options.why: A flat denial is a promise the next leak can break.

options.text: The board and I are talking. I'm not going anywhere today.
headlines: Rare calm statement confuses cable news
options.why: A small, true statement leaves nothing to debunk.

options.text: Have you SEEN our quarterly numbers?
options.why: Changing the subject works until someone repeats the question.

options.text: *puts on sunglasses, walks straight into a server rack*
options.why: Going viral is not the same as being believed.

rounds.question: Did you know about the internal investigation?

options.text: I found out about it from your article.
headlines: Email shows CEO was cc'd in March
'Found out from your article' now a meme
options.why: If a paper trail exists, 'I didn't know' becomes the story.

options.text: Yes. I cooperated, and I'll keep cooperating.
options.why: Admitting the knowable fact takes the leak's power away.

options.text: Investigations are how great companies stay great.
headlines: Comms team adds 'stay great' to banned phrases
options.why: Corporate fog reads as hiding something.

options.text: The real investigation should be into who leaked this.
headlines: Staff start group chat called 'the real investigation'
options.why: Going after the leaker confirms the leak is real.

rounds.question: Will the shake-up change your China plans?

options.text: Honestly? China is our favourite customer.
headlines: Senators draft angry letter in record time
options.why: A line written for one audience is heard by all of them.

options.text: We follow every export rule, in every country. Nothing changes.
headlines: Nobody clips it, which is the point
options.why: Boring and checkable beats exciting and quotable.

options.text: No comment. But I love dumplings.
headlines: State TV runs 'he loves dumplings' on loop
options.why: A joke is still a quote, and quotes travel without context.

options.text: If they fire me, China wins.
headlines: Chinese government is looking for you
Washington is also looking for you
options.why: Fear works as a headline and fails as an argument.

options.text: Quote-post: "Watching is free. Our chips are not."
options.why: Winning the reply can cost you the relationship.

options.text: "We spoke this morning. Shipments are on schedule."
options.why: A checkable fact ends a vague rumour faster than a comeback.

options.text: Announce a surprise product: the Jacket GPU.
headlines: Board learns about product from social media
options.why: A shiny distraction buys a news cycle, not trust.

options.text: Say nothing for 72 hours.
options.why: When you leave a gap, someone else fills it.

rounds.question: The board is in the room. Last words?

options.text: I made mistakes. I'll own them, whatever the board decides.
options.why: Owning it early is cheaper than being caught later.

options.text: This company IS me. Remove me and it collapses.
options.why: Making it about yourself proves the board's point.

options.text: "Thank you all. Any questions? No? Great." *leaves*
headlines: Reporters still shouting at empty podium
options.why: Dodging on camera is itself the footage.

options.text: I'm stepping back to focus on my jacket collection.
options.why: Self-mockery lowers the temperature. It doesn't answer the question.

own.why: Plain and true leaves nothing to debunk.

deny.why: Every denial is a promise the next leak can break.

deflect.why: Reporters repeat the question. Viewers notice.

attack.why: Attacking the messenger tells everyone the message was real.

headlines: Clip goes viral, problem does not go away
joke.why: Jokes win the clip, not the argument.

hype.why: Big numbers move the stock, not the story.

vague.why: Corporate fog reads as hiding something.

endings.headline: STILL THE CEO.
endings.dek: He survives the cycle. The jacket stays on.

endings.headline: OUSTED, BELOVED.
endings.dek: Fired on Friday. Booked for three keynotes by Monday.

endings.headline: THE INTERIM ERA BEGINS.
endings.dek: He keeps the title. Someone else gets the keys.

endings.headline: OUSTED.
endings.dek: The board has accepted a resignation he never offered.

lessons.own: Small true statements gave the leaks nothing to find.
lessons.deny: Every denial became a promise the next leak could break.
lessons.deflect: Changing the subject works once. Reporters repeat the question.
lessons.attack: Attacking the messenger told everyone the message was real.
lessons.joke: Jokes won the clip, not the argument.
lessons.hype: Big numbers moved the stock, not the story.
lessons.vague: Corporate fog read as hiding something.
